title: How Workers Struggle in America’s Dead-End Economy
author: Roxanne D. Brown
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/IMG_0556-680x510.jpeg)

Photograph by Nathaniel St. Clair

It’s common to see members of the United Steelworkers (USW) retire after
dedicating their entire working lives to a single mill or plant.

They deliver decades of skill and experience to an employer. In return, they
receive the security of a USW contract, including steady pay, quality health
care, fair treatment and strong retirement plans that carry them through their
golden years.

This is how a healthy system functions—one generation driving prosperity and
empowering the next to continue the fight. It’s the American dream.

But today, the notion of the American dream is coming apart at the seams. Tens
of millions of workers find only a [dead-end
economy](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BCLSxZMIaCgsuN1-2Bpde0MRW0F77c5ScYlBfqYfNkyp1ISR-2Fkgl3fKbWztuxFobbW3MP4AikTcCqNqQUzHizAeSVSiVB7ihLLQE6UGmvCqpynEiDgeVwI2Vru2gRoGiEUrQ-3D-3D7aly_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bsd55T98Nf4Mouz9Lb09iRqmm02J2zf5PNgi4BrhjOcwr41qLlvt3nYBqagtYCLiAjvCKyiT4uGAAlE0SE204c9ou2HcoAFPh7B-2FvYEyjyaFrTZCiaA9cjk2DEW2lvHrA-2Bc1RTIsYyJlBpTA7BeBo40pCz9luPsu3v9y5IIFTJAIMBFrxGYK1K7Vr1TKk6yftAFX62mmYRk2emO2qLSgJy5zzndmm2f1CBLaEAPZNgJnkcQi8a9NlldxU40Q8B6iXd0KwR2FRjnzw-2FZKZ85nsow-2F1rvjJo-2BCcw60ciVUBkCpzfU-2F7DRhSumIlC241K9GEPwQ6j-2Fl3ytUVQM0-2FmFfLvXvJ9AVDPyoOwGbkjHnPfwRVAZEMjXv2Zgv-2FyMuV1jm0gtxigYcKxkxynHdcKMP69Qnn7XLvj-2BpNPv90e8iCXkag2t26FnTiNBuHx7f7QO470Gk65vIfNNRZ02iSN3jgkIZnBAC8d4oJjUDeH1XNnc9YmRNOV-2F6xdmRHzX3B7gvDxY-2Fwhg-2BU4HzZq-2Bnx3hE1DcESlr0Sh2nXd9CkaStdVFx88T-2Fg00eL-2F9QPwXBxU1XJR-2B8DP9vRHw-2Bb50rKMg6z82Wzg7DxyMVNX5qx13GdWpUKovtSSx4dzMipxE5Y2vj-2Bt3GbNBNdazbib1GFJyF2LwaNRioG2lX2ZH0T0cRAEzF23KzhTsfAl6EYqCqJNHlmVXDTZ7-2FLKuHYAdFVQWmAdQ-2BdX2MMJmZmlEioswSVwms-3D)

These workers—from all ages, backgrounds, and parts of the country—simply
cannot find career-long, family- and community-sustaining jobs amid Trump
administration policies that
[choke](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BNaWOFV5IM0saoSqM3oEOjFcG-2BpQBM0t-2BDrzNTVHP1cGbBiKaYAUl9fNnQzZJ0vKES-2BqIf3lmS0A4JYpaTGYSQW4FEyaooJLE3g53i5mTA1Uw2544s0OMPJpDXsMrUboo9xXsySPQL3zTVcedVsE7KquGBOGLb90d0MTQeQH-2FrhdBtmM_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bsd55T98Nf4Mouz9Lb09iRqmm02J2zf5PNgi4BrhjOcwr41qLlvt3nYBqagtYCLiAjvCKyiT4uGAAlE0SE204c9ou2HcoAFPh7B-2FvYEyjyaFrTZCiaA9cjk2DEW2lvHrA-2Bc1RTIsYyJlBpTA7BeBo40pCz9luPsu3v9y5IIFTJAIMBFrxGYK1K7Vr1TKk6yftAFX62mmYRk2emO2qLSgJy5zzndmm2f1CBLaEAPZNgJnkcQi8a9NlldxU40Q8B6iXd0KwR2FRjnzw-2FZKZ85nsow-2F1rvjJo-2BCcw60ciVUBkCpzfU-2F7DRhSumIlC241K9GEPwQ6j-2Fl3ytUVQM0-2FmFfLvXvJ9AVDPyoOwGbkjHnPfwRVAZEMjXv2Zgv-2FyMuV1jm0gtxigYcKxkxynHdcKMP69Qnn7XLvj-2BpNPv90e8iCXkag2t26FnTiNBuHx7f7QO470Gk65vIfNNRZ02iSN3jgkIZnBAC8d4oJjUDeH1XNnc9YmRNOV-2F6xdmRHzX3B7gvDxY-2Fwhg-2BU4HzZq-2Bnx3hE1DVVxEF0Nu5metnLJIe6d2xhB-2FWMQ-2FB2j9PLZtRADQZCRWV-2BIqtfJT8t5wAFbe153IJIS6ylWFnIAfINYmOhBpBVQpcbAw-2FNRkk-2BcRdfR-2FWCu9ctI52Da9ZWXq83ipQNBkGtjOI36keXHXO59AoZtAglaBWDEEwmcHFpPMU5AtuayTSOF6W1fvXIkp71jbjwEfYDvCxPDJ3YjlIkMa6lynbs-3D)
investment and kill growth.

Instead, their backs are against the wall, and these workers have little
choice but to juggle multiple part-time jobs that provide neither the
opportunities they crave nor the wages, benefits, and security their families
require. Unable to get the jobs they want, they take whatever they can get and
try to make do.

About 54 million Americans now [draw incomes from multiple
sources](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BCKdTU3ksn3autqtCriX6-2Fh13j8nV6O-2BbbTEKp-2BuOFgxSUFkcnNsCUZZKiNrUu18ArSgOSwTj3XSbTbKAoXw8u9Aa0d-2BvJxjxlb-2BzTE3UjL8zd-2FO7PU5m2im1Xmrc23px7zQn5BiBHjMKCUQiyOZ8uM-3D7CHg_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bsd55T98Nf4Mouz9Lb09iRqmm02J2zf5PNgi4BrhjOcwr41qLlvt3nYBqagtYCLiAjvCKyiT4uGAAlE0SE204c9ou2HcoAFPh7B-2FvYEyjyaFrTZCiaA9cjk2DEW2lvHrA-2Bc1RTIsYyJlBpTA7BeBo40pCz9luPsu3v9y5IIFTJAIMBFrxGYK1K7Vr1TKk6yftAFX62mmYRk2emO2qLSgJy5zzndmm2f1CBLaEAPZNgJnkcQi8a9NlldxU40Q8B6iXd0KwR2FRjnzw-2FZKZ85nsow-2F1rvjJo-2BCcw60ciVUBkCpzfU-2F7DRhSumIlC241K9GEPwQ6j-2Fl3ytUVQM0-2FmFfLvXvJ9AVDPyoOwGbkjHnPfwRVAZEMjXv2Zgv-2FyMuV1jm0gtxigYcKxkxynHdcKMP69Qnn7XLvj-2BpNPv90e8iCXkag2t26FnTiNBuHx7f7QO470Gk65vIfNNRZ02iSN3jgkIZnBAC8d4oJjUDeH1XNnc9YmRNOV-2F6xdmRHzX3B7gvDxY-2Fwhg-2BU4HzZq-2Bnx3hE1DVEGzJWcGhjT3CJVWzVWjXSWkqOzqsznjGHLa8fvcJPBw2y4bjGISDR-2FEVyEknOwhOwecAA9TzDEOIxTDMTznmfrW9Nnr4qQzxS8pJxvrOoiFh964LbErs2eP-2BjFTRH-2FmVJSQa-2FaKvjwgiQikmc8XdoHW1lGyqjqLdMPwi0yl-2BdHoPhERTYG6ydHqCcXNuPmsGn4qZInXnoc-2Bn42EexPIDs-3D),

Researchers found the US worker’s gold standard—a “steady, predictable
paycheck”—increasingly giving way to income arriving in dribs and drabs at
“variable times.”

This isn’t living. It’s no longer the dream. It’s hanging on—and a world away
from the stability that hundreds of thousands of USW members still get in the
contracts they negotiate.

One woman threw the scope of the crisis into sharp relief when she went public
with her story earlier this year, writing that she and her husband have [10
jobs between the two of
them](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BMBUC69eKQee-2F-2FVb9cXZGUXgPny9Cmb1iUSW9w-2FyP4J-2FpulLIyPpkdDb3yMwcL4gxQzeldxSp4Wod0EM9sNkJnzCAgEXjtKrmN3L7nJsqZ-2Fjri1fFobIMmaLxieVOYW73g-3D-3DshPP_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bsd55T98Nf4Mouz9Lb09iRqmm02J2zf5PNgi4BrhjOcwr41qLlvt3nYBqagtYCLiAjvCKyiT4uGAAlE0SE204c9ou2HcoAFPh7B-2FvYEyjyaFrTZCiaA9cjk2DEW2lvHrA-2Bc1RTIsYyJlBpTA7BeBo40pCz9luPsu3v9y5IIFTJAIMBFrxGYK1K7Vr1TKk6yftAFX62mmYRk2emO2qLSgJy5zzndmm2f1CBLaEAPZNgJnkcQi8a9NlldxU40Q8B6iXd0KwR2FRjnzw-2FZKZ85nsow-2F1rvjJo-2BCcw60ciVUBkCpzfU-2F7DRhSumIlC241K9GEPwQ6j-2Fl3ytUVQM0-2FmFfLvXvJ9AVDPyoOwGbkjHnPfwRVAZEMjXv2Zgv-2FyMuV1jm0gtxigYcKxkxynHdcKMP69Qnn7XLvj-2BpNPv90e8iCXkag2t26FnTiNBuHx7f7QO470Gk65vIfNNRZ02iSN3jgkIZnBAC8d4oJjUDeH1XNnc9YmRNOV-2F6xdmRHzX3B7gvDxY-2Fwhg-2BU4HzZq-2Bnx3hE1DVoO61N1wzb4JI98CT7E0RlGlgAQJn4uceXHlHDe6Wi9yEauphZ-2FyklBemtOoueNBQuZrqv5FFrhbvwSGGDKasujYoKoWtJK6pz4PLXxpj5BZD8Be3u4xLTbuVJTRrVNl6qDWIWVI3G007fm7qzkqxzP5UyFe15jyRqYiP7Ui-2BCt1EkNQuqCmnImD0qVOnUW6dExrrOu-2BQmp3Vl58FXr3M0-3D)
but still struggle to raise five kids and pay the bills.

“The sobering realization that even 10 jobs isn’t enough is very defeating,”
she wrote. “I’m still working on a solution.”

How much more can she and her husband do?

They’re holding up their end. But instead of supporting them, the government
all but ignores so-called “income stackers” like these.

The nation’s official unemployment rate—[4.1 percent in
July](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BAYZ78nywrQAOoY9RR6hk9-2BdGo5kh1rkJt5n0BHXBJU0WgW1yd2H2lWyjKJKYJm9x8GZ-2BgesDXjC6hoHA98jlBM-3D0F7U_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bsd55T98Nf4Mouz9Lb09iRqmm02J2zf5PNgi4BrhjOcwr41qLlvt3nYBqagtYCLiAjvCKyiT4uGAAlE0SE204c9ou2HcoAFPh7B-2FvYEyjyaFrTZCiaA9cjk2DEW2lvHrA-2Bc1RTIsYyJlBpTA7BeBo40pCz9luPsu3v9y5IIFTJAIMBFrxGYK1K7Vr1TKk6yftAFX62mmYRk2emO2qLSgJy5zzndmm2f1CBLaEAPZNgJnkcQi8a9NlldxU40Q8B6iXd0KwR2FRjnzw-2FZKZ85nsow-2F1rvjJo-2BCcw60ciVUBkCpzfU-2F7DRhSumIlC241K9GEPwQ6j-2Fl3ytUVQM0-2FmFfLvXvJ9AVDPyoOwGbkjHnPfwRVAZEMjXv2Zgv-2FyMuV1jm0gtxigYcKxkxynHdcKMP69Qnn7XLvj-2BpNPv90e8iCXkag2t26FnTiNBuHx7f7QO470Gk65vIfNNRZ02iSN3jgkIZnBAC8d4oJjUDeH1XNnc9YmRNOV-2F6xdmRHzX3B7gvDxY-2Fwhg-2BU4HzZq-2Bnx3hE1DTxbY20wAIcWEsoLWMGw-2Ba637V5RrY4ccYqHrFsDdBHMcVppZ-2Bs8Xn3ZvUcYGur2etZWgIt48dLyBRg9kP6JWJROvc98JVAC4p92U-2B2XQKbMCLMJyFd3ue015090aiJlAHmJk5-2B8NmkEZMnyoln7NeYs635yO-2FgIX9CV-2Ff-2F-2Fp7U3uF6Wg6U-2FXDwJCVYm-2F04HvMoRrFXG6re44bDUVVqp5IQ-3D)—measures
only the number of Americans 16 and older who are unemployed and looking for
work.

It fails to count the skyrocketing number of people who work part-time against
their will and barely scrape by. As a result, the unemployment rate offers a
gerrymandered view of the economy, making conditions look healthier than
people know them to be.

After adding up all of those out of work and all of those working less than
they want, analyst Gene Ludwig concluded that [nearly 25 percent of
Americans](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BPrMnffi8cH9XOIpi62ZdD7IiNujx7I-2BOjYHBKN0NeDDDoFjqKmgN185Bgjvx3dybJ-2ByrwCCBUJXkGr3y2tavznfMBJUzbURvMXHqou5-2FY3-2BDosy_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bsd55T98Nf4Mouz9Lb09iRqmm02J2zf5PNgi4BrhjOcwr41qLlvt3nYBqagtYCLiAjvCKyiT4uGAAlE0SE204c9ou2HcoAFPh7B-2FvYEyjyaFrTZCiaA9cjk2DEW2lvHrA-2Bc1RTIsYyJlBpTA7BeBo40pCz9luPsu3v9y5IIFTJAIMBFrxGYK1K7Vr1TKk6yftAFX62mmYRk2emO2qLSgJy5zzndmm2f1CBLaEAPZNgJnkcQi8a9NlldxU40Q8B6iXd0KwR2FRjnzw-2FZKZ85nsow-2F1rvjJo-2BCcw60ciVUBkCpzfU-2F7DRhSumIlC241K9GEPwQ6j-2Fl3ytUVQM0-2FmFfLvXvJ9AVDPyoOwGbkjHnPfwRVAZEMjXv2Zgv-2FyMuV1jm0gtxigYcKxkxynHdcKMP69Qnn7XLvj-2BpNPv90e8iCXkag2t26FnTiNBuHx7f7QO470Gk65vIfNNRZ02iSN3jgkIZnBAC8d4oJjUDeH1XNnc9YmRNOV-2F6xdmRHzX3B7gvDxY-2Fwhg-2BU4HzZq-2Bnx3hE1DZhwVuSoHlvTx1XE63qtuv12QejKFLNmqIrwkKRikVAxr1FsOMPIp-2BVUAXIbykzMMVcW-2FD1JFp6tqS-2FvC-2FldJAndqQWYASGKBr7SShKyQwdz4t2aN8NFzcjsm69uY-2BuRers-2FUVJQSguFDBxemK7sRJkjUxtR1MLWxEB3yoeF3RNiMKuoUurj-2BFgEISi4Po8phT8EBBhS1V7b33RGvrYukBM-3D)
are “functionally unemployed.”

In other words, we sidelined a huge swath of the workforce, leaving no
suitable outlet for their skills, no way to parlay those skills into adequate
income, and no path forward.

Little wonder that [members of this burgeoning
underclass](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BDov8u6CFAWZv6uQtvzo8QXDSGaZ6aU89Z3-2BHxhbGNDqfw-2B3gDVMi42KSgJxShPlTMUCm85CuquIIFRi8FHpShamWuTAFYnLxn41LRwcss7whmAd_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bsd55T98Nf4Mouz9Lb09iRqmm02J2zf5PNgi4BrhjOcwr41qLlvt3nYBqagtYCLiAjvCKyiT4uGAAlE0SE204c9ou2HcoAFPh7B-2FvYEyjyaFrTZCiaA9cjk2DEW2lvHrA-2Bc1RTIsYyJlBpTA7BeBo40pCz9luPsu3v9y5IIFTJAIMBFrxGYK1K7Vr1TKk6yftAFX62mmYRk2emO2qLSgJy5zzndmm2f1CBLaEAPZNgJnkcQi8a9NlldxU40Q8B6iXd0KwR2FRjnzw-2FZKZ85nsow-2F1rvjJo-2BCcw60ciVUBkCpzfU-2F7DRhSumIlC241K9GEPwQ6j-2Fl3ytUVQM0-2FmFfLvXvJ9AVDPyoOwGbkjHnPfwRVAZEMjXv2Zgv-2FyMuV1jm0gtxigYcKxkxynHdcKMP69Qnn7XLvj-2BpNPv90e8iCXkag2t26FnTiNBuHx7f7QO470Gk65vIfNNRZ02iSN3jgkIZnBAC8d4oJjUDeH1XNnc9YmRNOV-2F6xdmRHzX3B7gvDxY-2Fwhg-2BU4HzZq-2Bnx3hE1DRqJ-2FE3184KxiL6XPAS-2F5Z9pNnuaCIt3v1igLXUnhnVd-2B7InAk5wEgVGD4ph-2B9Ll1zwTehN-2B2wbSgJVqFDvTfMOGpuuyPOTMk9fv17-2F3k3Q8RbI42PWcGiHHNeOWTRmzLZg970eBPhlvGvLG37IegELyIdz0hhD5qP55whFR3F3x8Avq0Orl8UJhTakctZVjT-2BoDuskProQVqXFj5EDHcMA-3D)
describe themselves as feeling “defeated,” “stuck,” and “sick of trying.” They
characterize the job market as “truly abysmal,” “very bleak,” and a “[mental
war](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BIlQ-2BIu8o1ARjNEGIjuYcYpSS54oEELz6ePXBqeNcpNIzdrjTO-2FCnLdex9dOcmGW5-2FNDf1AoN5lJea8IfKYMAnQWe1y3ABv9BdGtJ7ELz6OFLO5YLopgqcbPwmpZAotp9w-3D-3D_9tZ_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bsd55T98Nf4Mouz9Lb09iRqmm02J2zf5PNgi4BrhjOcwr41qLlvt3nYBqagtYCLiAjvCKyiT4uGAAlE0SE204c9ou2HcoAFPh7B-2FvYEyjyaFrTZCiaA9cjk2DEW2lvHrA-2Bc1RTIsYyJlBpTA7BeBo40pCz9luPsu3v9y5IIFTJAIMBFrxGYK1K7Vr1TKk6yftAFX62mmYRk2emO2qLSgJy5zzndmm2f1CBLaEAPZNgJnkcQi8a9NlldxU40Q8B6iXd0KwR2FRjnzw-2FZKZ85nsow-2F1rvjJo-2BCcw60ciVUBkCpzfU-2F7DRhSumIlC241K9GEPwQ6j-2Fl3ytUVQM0-2FmFfLvXvJ9AVDPyoOwGbkjHnPfwRVAZEMjXv2Zgv-2FyMuV1jm0gtxigYcKxkxynHdcKMP69Qnn7XLvj-2BpNPv90e8iCXkag2t26FnTiNBuHx7f7QO470Gk65vIfNNRZ02iSN3jgkIZnBAC8d4oJjUDeH1XNnc9YmRNOV-2F6xdmRHzX3B7gvDxY-2Fwhg-2BU4HzZq-2Bnx3hE1DaEMoYnlGx9k5hSK4LkLMP05NXd-2FbVEEW0FV-2Fojf0Lw23w3KafzUVJ5sQbE-2BHSa-2Faw-2Bkx0gd0JpGeSABrturgBvYgwS11OGgE4hU02WM9nac89kRrUKm2yuwYYSyMuELT7f6ZilKSKhsqNviUzkuSvOKvy-2F21uorGPOaFJU-2B8a0xAjliZ0JDqpCGX4CxhDvYthFrb2UPQsImA3OFKYjFX3s-3D).”

The current administration owns this mess.
